label.en: Stage: riddles end stage (other side proactive) (difficulty 5) / riddles end stage (other side cautious) (difficulty 7)

texts.zh: 尽管我们一开始在演绎推导[This.ContactCountry.GetName]所使用的语言的基础取得了些许的成功，之后我们在建立与他们有意义的交流进程中却停滞不前。似乎他们在讲一种奇怪的谜语，通过某种精悍但不是很有意义的短语来传递意义，我们只能猜测其其重要性。
texts.en: After some initial successes in deducing the fundamentals of the language used by the [This.ContactCountry.GetName], our progress in establishing meaningful communications with them has stalled. It appears that they speak in strange riddles, somehow conveying meaning through short and seemingly nonsensical phrases of which we can only guess the significance.

label.zh: 令人疑惑。我们需要收集更大的样本量。
label.en: Puzzling. We will need to gather a larger sample size.

label.zh: 进入阶段：谜语收尾阶段（对方主动）(难度5) / 谜语收尾阶段（对方谨慎）(难度7)
label.en: Stage: riddles end stage (other side proactive) (difficulty 5) / riddles end stage (other side cautious) (difficulty 7)

texts.zh:
随着我们进一步调查[This.ContactCountry.GetName]——我们现在知道是[This.ContactCountry.GetRealName]——我们终于知道他们使用的短语常常用典于在过去一些时间点上发生的重大的、知名的事件。这些典故的意味在他们族人内部显然是广为人知的，可以用于表达一种情感，或描述事务的状态。

幸运的是，看上去这种形式的语言并不是唯一的版本，仅仅作为“高端腔”，用于官方的场合或者智者之间的交流。一种更加广泛的“低端腔”文法在非正式的场合被频繁使用，特别是在年轻人或者文化水平不高的人之间。不幸的是，同一个地位颇高的人使用“低端腔”交流是一件非常具有侮辱意味的事情，我们要是这样同他们沟通，他们准把我们当作智力等同于小孩的物种来对待……
texts.en:
As we continued to investigate the [This.ContactCountry.GetName] - who we now know to be the [This.ContactCountry.GetRealName] - it became clear that the phrases they use are references to significant, well-known events that happened at some point in their past. The meanings of these references are apparently generally recognized among their kind, and can be a shorthand for expressing a sentiment or state of affairs.

Fortunately, it seems that this form of their language is not the only version of it, but merely the "high speech", used in official settings and between intellectuals. An altogether more comprehensible "low speech" vernacular is used in more informal settings, especially among the young and those of lesser intelligence. Unfortunately, it is considered gravely insulting to speak to one of high standing using the "low speech", so that they must treat us as the intellectual equivalents of children in order to communicate with us...

texts.zh:
随着我们对其调查的深入，[This.ContactCountry.GetName]——现在我们知道叫[This.ContactCountry.GetRealName]——他们使用的语句其实是某种我们未获取秘钥的编码。显然它们指的是在我们[This.ContactCountry.GetSpeciesNamePlural]之间共享的知识的事件，可能是表达情感或事态的简写。

幸运的是，他们并不是总用这种“高级语言”来交流，除非是在沟通重要的事项。一种并行的更易理解的“低级语言”则被运用于非正式的场合，特别是年轻个体和低智力个体间。然而，看起来那些高等个体们对“低级语言”使用者嗤之以鼻，也就是说他们可能把我们当做智力等同于孩童一般与我们进行交流……
texts.en:
As we continued to investigate the [This.ContactCountry.GetName] - who we now know to be the [This.ContactCountry.GetRealName] - it became clear that the phrases they use are some sort of code to which we lack the key. Apparently they refer to events that are shared knowledge among the [This.ContactCountry.GetSpeciesNamePlural], and can be a shorthand for expressing a sentiment or state of affairs.

Fortunately, it seems that they do not always communicate in such a manner but merely use this "high speech" when important matters are being discussed. An altogether more comprehensible "low speech" vernacular is used in more informal settings, especially among the young and those of lesser intelligence. Unfortunately, it seems that those of high standing react with scorn to those using the "low speech", meaning that they must treat us as the intellectual equivalents of children in order to communicate with us...

label.zh: 懂了，这就用“低端腔”同他们对线。
我们肯定可以讲他们真正的语言。
label.en: Surely we can manage to speak their true language.

notes.zh: 审阅注：355 是谜语链的收尾阶段事件。选项A（用“低级语言”）直接结束并得到“不太聪明”的意见修正；选项B进入356，用对方的“真正语言”打招呼。
notes.en: Review note: 355 is the riddles end-stage event. Option A (the "low speech") finishes at once with a not-very-intelligent opinion modifier; option B opens 356 to greet them in their true language.

texts.zh: [This.Owner.GetEnvoyCap][This.Leader.GetName]顿了顿，看上去很迷惑。我们从他们信息的开头采集了几个短语。我们应该怎么和他们打招呼？
texts.en: [This.Owner.GetEnvoyCap] [This.Leader.GetName] pauses, looking confused. We have gathered several phrases that they seem to begin their messages with. Which should we use to greet them?

tooltips.zh: 如果我们使用了正确的致敬，[This.ContactCountry.GetSpeciesNamePlural]会对我们非常印象深刻，但是如果用错了他们会感觉有被冒犯到。
tooltips.en: If we use the correct greeting, the [This.ContactCountry.GetSpeciesNamePlural] will be most impressed, but using the wrong one will likely cause offense.

tooltips.zh: 如果我们使用了正确的致敬，[This.ContactCountry.GetSpeciesNamePlural]会对我们非常印象深刻，但是如果用错了他们会感觉有被冒犯到。
tooltips.en: If we use the correct greeting, the [This.ContactCountry.GetSpeciesNamePlural] will be most impressed, but using the wrong one will likely cause offense.

label.zh: 三思，这事还是保险一点好。
label.en: Better to play this safe, on second thought.

notes.zh: 审阅注：356 的 immediate 随机设定 option_A_correct / option_B_correct 之一（各50%）；选对的问候语→357，选错→358；选项C放弃并结束。
notes.en: Review note: 356 randomly sets option_A_correct or option_B_correct (50/50) in its immediate block; the matching greeting leads to 357, the other to 358; option C gives up and finishes.

texts.zh: 我们的发言得到了立即的反应。微笑——至少我们相信是和微笑类似的表情——在[This.ContactCountry.GetSpeciesNamePlural]间洋溢开来，他们嘴里讲了几个短语，用的是不容置喙的友好的字词。看上去我们选择致敬的方式选对了。
texts.en: The reaction to our words was instantaneous. Smiles - or at least, what we believe to be their equivalent of smiles - broke out among the [This.ContactCountry.GetSpeciesNamePlural], who uttered several phrases of unmistakably friendly character. It seems we chose our form of greeting well.

label.zh: 这是一群令人愉悦的人。
这是一群令人愉悦的人。
他们不将我们视作没有价值的人，这是好事。
label.en: It is well that they should not see us as unworthy.

label.zh: 我们可以借此了解更多关于他们的信息。
label.en: We can leverage this to find out more about them.

tooltips.en: Gain +25% spy network growth on the [This.ContactCountry.GetRealName]

note.zh: 对方留下好印象（语言一致加成）；可选“深入了解”改为获得间谍网加成。
note.en: Good impression and a 25-year speak-like-us bonus; option C instead grants a spy-network modifier.

texts.zh:
话语刚一说出口，很明显我们就选错了。[This.ContactCountry.GetSpeciesNamePlural]保持了很长一段的沉默，接着我们遭到了如连珠炮一般措辞强烈的谴责。他们的意图很明显带有敌意，即便他们想要表达的准确意味尚不明确——我们本来打算着让[This.ContactCountry.GetSpeciesNamePlural]印象深刻，结果是我们羞辱了他们。

往好处看，至少我们现在能和他们沟通了，某种程度上。
texts.en:
As soon as the words were uttered, it was obvious that we had chosen poorly. The [This.ContactCountry.GetSpeciesNamePlural] held their silence for a long moment before we were beset by a barrage of harshly-spoken phrases. Their intent is clearly hostile, even if their exact meaning remains unclear - it seems that in our attempt to impress the [This.ContactCountry.GetSpeciesNamePlural], we only manage to insult them.

On the positive side, at least we are able to communicate with them now, to some degree.

note.zh: 对方非常被冒犯（very insulting 意见修正）。
note.en: They are deeply insulted (opinion modifier very_insulting).

summary.text:
# 谜语人 / Speaking in Riddles
- 分类 Category：文明纪事 Society (C7) · 首次接触阶段链 first-contact stage chain（首个事件「谜语人」first_contact.350）
- 来源 Sources：`events/first_contact_events.txt:4908–5180` · `common/first_contact/00_first_contact.txt:453–486, 1544–1581`
- 审阅 Reviewed：2026-10-13（c7b-society）

## 如何开始 How it starts

首次接触第二阶段（default_stage_2）按权重抽取故事线；“谜语人”权重 5，若本方已有此链标记 first_contact_speaking_in_riddles_chain、本方为格式塔且已与常规帝国通讯、本方或对方为“灭绝”倾向、或对方为格式塔，则权重为 0（`00_first_contact.txt:454–486`）。/ In stage 2 the game draws one storyline by weight; Speaking in Riddles has weight 5 and is excluded once the empire has had the chain, for gestalt observers who already talk to a regular empire, for homicidal empires, or gestalt contacts.

## 剧情脉络 Story outline

1. **谜语人（350）**：单一选项，根据对方的首次接触政策进入“谜语收尾阶段”（对方主动：难度5；否则：难度7）。/ One option; the other empire’s policy picks the proactive (difficulty 5) or cautious (difficulty 7) end stage.
2. **一种隐喻语言（355）**（阶段完成后触发）：A 用“低级语言”接触并结束；B → 356。/ After the stage completes, A finishes with the low speech; B goes on to 356.
3. **联系对方（356）**：随机决定两种问候语中哪一种“正确”（各 50%），选A或B → 说对 357 / 说错 358；C 放弃。/ A random coin decides which of two greetings is right; a right choice leads to 357, a wrong one to 358; C gives up.

## 分支与结局 Branches and outcomes

- 357：说对 → 良好印象；选项 C 另得间谍网加成。/ Right greeting: good impression, option C grants a spy-network modifier.
- 358：说错 → 极大冒犯。/ Wrong greeting: they are very insulted.
- 355.A、356.C：以“不太聪明”意见修正直接结束。/ 355.A and 356.C end with a not-very-intelligent opinion modifier.
- 所有收尾选项都调用 finish_first_contact_effect（建立正式通讯，之后按帝国类型转入后续事件，如反向接触、教程、商队等），并调用 first_contact_inform_intel。 / Every ending option calls finish_first_contact_effect (opens regular communications, then routes to follow-ups such as reverse first contact, tutorial, caravaneer events) and first_contact_inform_intel.

## 条件与文明差异 Conditions and variants

355 的文本对格式塔与非格式塔不同；357 的选项文字按排外与否变化。/ 355 has gestalt and non-gestalt text; 357’s option text depends on xenophobia.

## 审阅记录 Review notes

- 已核对 Checked：350–358 全部脚本、default_stage_2 条目、两个谜语收尾阶段（`00_first_contact.txt:1544–1581`）。/ Scripts 350–358, the stage-2 entry and both end-stage definitions.
- 审阅改动 Changes：原先 355 单独成篇，350 混在“难以捉摸的外星人”中；现用阶段连接把 350→355 串成一棵树并并入本篇（story event-first-contact-355 现含 350）。/ 355 used to be a separate story and 350 sat in the stage-2 pile; a stage bridge now links 350 → 355 and both live here.
- 注意 Note：阶段完成后的触发是“进度检定”，成功才触发该事件；失败时按 on_roll_failed 的随机池处理（谜语收尾阶段失败池为 no_events 之外的设置见阶段定义）。/ A stage fires its event only when its progress roll succeeds; failures go through the stage’s on_roll_failed pool.
